requirement:
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
rationale:
`requirements.references.outline_selectors` says Habeas uses the outline selector grammar under `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses. That grammar is cited context, so I did not reassess its own tests. I checked that the marked tests apply it to Habeas's source addresses.

- **Named segments, nesting, and the empty selector.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` builds many Rust selectors, such as `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`, and `extern[C]/fn[puts]`. It asserts that each selector is emitted and that `resolve` maps it back to the same node. It also asserts that `resolve("")` returns the root.
- **Percent-encoding.** The same test uses `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]/fn[edge]`, so brackets and spaces are encoded. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent]` asserts that a malformed escape (`fn[bad%ZZ]`) returns `ResolveError::Invalid` with a "malformed percent escape" message. It also asserts that a missing node returns the exact "no outline node matches" message.
- **`#N` disambiguation.** `fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` checks `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`, and that the bare `fn[repeated]` fails to resolve. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` checks `#1` and `#2` on two identical `use` items.
- **Anonymous `kind@hash` with 12 hex digits.** `fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` asserts the `use@` prefix and a length of 4 + 12. It asserts that old selectors still resolve after an unrelated insertion, and that an edit to the item makes the old selector fail. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits]` checks the `item@<first 12 of identity_hash>` form and that it survives a descendant edit. In the Markdown test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs#fn[paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges]`, every node's selector resolves back to itself and its segment has the `kind@` plus 12-digit shape.
- **Interchangeable `line` selectors.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` asserts that the two identical lines get the same selector and that it resolves.
- **No line numbers.** The selector shapes asserted above contain none, and the insertion test shows that selectors stay stable when line positions shift.
- **Use as source addresses.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reading_paths]` accepts valid selectors (empty, `fn[kept]`, `mod[a%2Fb]/fn[kept]`) in an `OutlineId`. It rejects `fn[missing`, `fn[bad%ZZ]`, and a leading `/`, and it checks that the path is not used for validation.

The other `{impl}` sites are `src/inputs.rs#impl[ParsedSource]/fn[resolve]` (maps resolution errors to messages), `src/authoring/tools.rs#impl[SearchNodes]/fn[entries]` (emits `node.selector`), and `Builder::finish` (assigns selectors). They only pass through or format values that the tests above exercise. `ParsedSource::resolve` is also exercised by tests that mark other requirements, so any gap there would be a marking gap rather than an assertion gap. I found no uncovered obligation or boundary named in the subject's text, and no acknowledgments were needed.

text: An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
